latest_implementation.selected_goal_name: Fixed Isometric Camera and Projection Setup
latest_implementation.selected_goal_description: Replace the disposable perspective test camera with a fixed orthographic isometric camera configuration matching the GDD's Diablo-1/Ultima-Online-inspired fixed 2.5D isometric presentation.
latest_implementation.implementation_summary: This was a refine pass on the previously-implemented orthographic isometric camera, correcting two human-Unity-runtime-reported defects without broadening scope. Root cause of "faces wrong direction": BuildCamera() set the camera's rotation (Euler 30,45,0) and its world position offset (10,10,-10) as two independently hand-picked values that did not actually agree - the forward vector produced by that rotation points away from the origin on the X axis rather than back toward it, so the camera's boresight missed the scene. Fix: the camera position is now derived directly from its own rotation (`targetPosition + rotation * new Vector3(0,0,-distance)`), i.e. it is placed by stepping back along its own local -Z axis from the follow target, which mathematically guarantees camera.forward always points exactly at the target regardless of the chosen angle - eliminating the class of bug entirely rather than just re-tuning magic numbers. Distance was kept equal to the original offset's magnitude (sqrt(300)) to preserve the same framing/zoom feel. Root cause of "stationary camera cripples gameplay": the camera had a one-time fixed world position with no tracking of the player. Fix: added a new IsometricCameraFollow component that stores a captured offset (camera position minus target position at Initialize time) and re-applies `target.position + offset` every LateUpdate, translating the camera each frame while never touching its rotation - preserving the fixed isometric orientation and preventing any free/player-controlled rotation, per the evaluator's developer_interpretation. BuildCamera() is now called after BuildPlayer() (minimal reordering) so it can wire the player's transform as the follow target, and the follow component is initialized via an explicit `Initialize()` call (not Awake) to avoid a component-lifecycle ordering pitfall where AddComponent invokes Awake before a caller-assigned target field would be set.
tests_added: Build_MainCamera_ForwardDirectionPointsAtPlayer - asserts the angle between camera.transform.forward and the direction to the player is under 0.5 degrees, directly catching the previous position/rotation mismatch bug

Build_MainCamera_HasFollowComponentTargetingPlayer - asserts an IsometricCameraFollow component exists on Main Camera and its private target field (read via SerializedObject, matching this test file's existing convention) is the Player transform

Build_MainCamera_TranslatesWithPlayerButRotationStaysFixed - moves the player, invokes the follow component's private LateUpdate via reflection (Unity does not run Update/LateUpdate outside Play Mode), and asserts the camera keeps the same relative offset to the player while its rotation is byte-for-byte unchanged

validations.name: Manual math verification of camera-forward-to-target alignment
validations.details: Verified analytically that position = target + rotation*(0,0,-distance) is algebraically equivalent to target - forward*distance (since forward = rotation*(0,0,1) and quaternion rotation distributes over scalar multiples), which guarantees camera.transform.forward points exactly at the target with zero angular error. This directly fixes the reported wrong-direction defect at its root cause.

Confirmed the diff contains exactly the intended camera fix and follow wiring, no stray edits.

requirements_satisfied: Camera remains orthographic (unchanged from the passing part of the prior implementation).

Camera rotation remains the fixed 30/45 dimetric isometric angle and is never modified after scene build, satisfying 'no free player-controlled rotation' and 'consistent isometric viewing orientation'.

Corrected the camera's world position so it is mathematically derived from its own rotation, fixing the reported 'view points in the wrong direction' defect at its root cause rather than re-guessing offset numbers.

Added camera translation/follow behavior (IsometricCameraFollow) so the player/gameplay area stays visible as the player moves, fixing the reported 'stationary camera cripples gameplay' defect, while explicitly not adding any rotation logic.

latest_evaluation.summary: The refined camera implementation (pass 2) correctly addresses both human-reported runtime defects while preserving orthographic projection, a fixed isometric orientation, and no free player-controlled rotation, and stays within the selected camera/projection scope.

criteria_results.evidence: DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.BuildCamera() sets camera.orthographic = true and camera.orthographicSize = IsometricOrthographicSize (8f) at lines 127-128, unchanged by this refine pass.

Camera rotation is fixed to Quaternion.Euler(30f,45f,0f) (IsometricCameraEulerAngles, line 22) and is set once in BuildCamera and never modified afterward (IsometricCameraFollow.LateUpdate only writes transform.position, never transform.rotation). The prior wrong-direction defect is fixed at the root: cameraObject.transform.position is now derived as targetPosition + rotation * new Vector3(0,0,-distance) (line 134), which is algebraically equivalent to targetPosition - camera.forward*distance, guaranteeing camera.forward points exactly at the target for any chosen rotation. A new test (Build_MainCamera_ForwardDirectionPointsAtPlayer) directly asserts the angle between camera.forward and the direction to the player is under 0.5 degrees.

IsometricCameraFollow (Scripts/IsometricCameraFollow.cs) only reads target.position and writes transform.position in LateUpdate; it never touches transform.rotation. No PlayerMovement, input, or other script in Assets/NoSafeCircle references camera rotation, and a grep for Orbit/FreeLook/MouseLook/CameraRotate across Assets/NoSafeCircle returns only the pre-existing test assertion that no such component is attached (Build_MainCamera_IsFixedOrthographicIsometric). New test Build_MainCamera_TranslatesWithPlayerButRotationStaysFixed explicitly asserts camera rotation is byte-for-byte unchanged after the player moves and the follow component runs.

Diff for this pass is confined to DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.cs (camera position/rotation fix + BuildCamera call reordered after BuildPlayer to obtain a follow target + follow-component wiring), a new IsometricCameraFollow.cs script (camera-follow-target scope), and the corresponding test file. No Tilemap, sprite-sorting, spell, enemy, or door-lifecycle code was touched; the camera-follow behavior added is explicitly the translation needed to keep the selected camera usable per the contract's own scope note ('Camera translation/follow needed to make the selected camera usable is still camera scope').

compile_risks: No Unity executable was available to actually compile/run the project (acknowledged honestly in implementation_result.json as unity_run_status: not_available); static review found no stale references to removed APIs, and the Tests.Editor asmdef already references the NoSafeCircle.DoorPrototype assembly where IsometricCameraFollow lives, so no reference-resolution issue is evident, but this remains unverified by an actual Unity compile.
non_blocking_notes: The runtime_feedback in ger_contract.json is fully addressed: the wrong-direction defect is fixed by deriving camera position from its own rotation rather than an independently hand-picked offset, and the stationary-camera defect is fixed by IsometricCameraFollow translating (never rotating) the camera to track the player.

Human Unity execution (Play Mode visual check, Test Runner run) is still required per remaining_work in implementation_result.json and per this GER's own rule that static evaluation is a separate layer from real Unity runtime validation; this pass does not claim otherwise.

runtime_feedback_used.summary: The orthographic camera implementation passed static evaluation but failed when tested in Unity: the view points in the wrong direction and the stationary camera makes gameplay unusable as the player moves.
runtime_feedback_used.developer_interpretation: For this implementation, preserve orthographic projection, a consistent isometric viewing orientation, and no free player-controlled rotation. Do not require the camera to stay at one absolute world-space position if translation/follow behavior is needed to keep gameplay visible.

blocking_issues.issue: The rebuilt orthographic camera faces the wrong direction.
blocking_issues.required_fix: Correct the isometric viewing direction/framing while preserving orthographic projection and a consistent isometric orientation.

blocking_issues.issue: The camera remains stationary while the player moves, causing the player/gameplay area to leave the useful view and crippling gameplay.
blocking_issues.required_fix: Keep the player/gameplay area visible through camera translation or follow behavior while preserving the fixed isometric orientation and preventing free player-controlled camera rotation.
